verses.verse:
न्यूनाधिक्येन छिद्राणाम् वंशी भेदोऽत्र लिख्यते।
षट्छिद्रा सप्तछिद्रा च तथाष्ट नव छिद्रिका।४१।
verses.text: Here the kinds of bānsurī by fewer or more holes are written down: six-holed, seven-holed, and likewise eight- and nine-holed.

commentary.text: Broadly, the bānsurī is of three kinds. (1) The Jihvāvatī, in which a jibbhī (fipple) is fitted. (2) The Kṛṣṇā bānsurī, in which a round mukharandhra (mouth-hole) is made. (3) The Tripurā, in which no separate hole is made for blowing and one has to blow through the natural opening itself; it is also called the prākṛta (natural) bānsurī. But here, on the basis of fewer or more holes, four kinds each of all the bānsurīs named above are being described.

# Ṣaṭchidrā (six-hole bānsurī) - in which the work of 12 notes is done with only 6 holes.
# Saptachidrā (seven-hole bānsurī) - in which 12 notes are arranged in 7 holes.
# Aṣṭachidrā (eight-hole bānsurī) - in which 12 notes are arranged in 8 holes.
# Navachidrā (nine-hole bānsurī) - in which 12 notes are arranged in 9 holes.

terms.en: six-hole bānsurī (twelve svaras from six holes)
